// Inefficient processing of term vectors during integrity checks
reader.checkIntegrity();
```
Reason:
The `checkIntegrity()` method was not optimized for handling term vectors, leading to longer execution times when processing indexes that contain term vectors. This inefficiency was particularly pronounced during the integrity checks, which were not tailored for term vector scenarios.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
long startIntegrityNS = System.nanoTime();
msg(infoStream, String.format(Locale.ROOT, "OK [took %.3f sec]", nsToSec(System.nanoTime()-startIntegrityNS)));
```
Reason:
The addition of timing measurements around the integrity check allows for better performance tracking and optimization. By measuring the time taken for the integrity check, developers can identify bottlenecks and optimize the process specifically for term vectors, thus speeding up the `CheckIndex` process.
